newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ICI Australia mulls petrochem plant.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ICI Australia mulls petrochem plant.

text.p: ICI Australia Ltd is considering building a A$2 billion petrochemicals plant in Western Australia to use natural gas from the North West Shelf project, the Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Friday.

Chief executive Warren Haynes was quoted as saying the project, if it proceeded, would probably be done in partnership. "It's a huge project. It will be export oriented. A world-scale plant would cost A$2 billion," he was quoted as saying.

The newspaper said ICI is considering a plant because it needs a new source of vinyl chloride monomer (VCM), the building block of poly-vinyl chloride (PVC), following the recent closure of its old Botany VCM plant in Sydney.
Haynes said ICI was planning to re-establish a local source of VCM, but warned that it was not a short-term project.
"There may be an opportunity in the North West Shelf and we're having a look at that, but it's a ways off," he said.
Australia consumes about 200,000 tonnes of VCM a year, which produces about the same quantity of PVC. This would leave about 300,0000 tonnes of VCM available for export, the newspaper said.

However, it said the plan depended on sufficient quantities of ethane being available at commercial prices from the North-West Shelf project. ICI Australia is 62.4 percent owned by Imperial Chemical Industries Plc.
